subset.rationale: tl::expected<T,E> is the library's whole point, bound head-on as two real specializations (int/std::string value-or-error and the role-swapped std::string/int): default + copy ctors, has_value(), explicit operator bool -> __bool__, the all-defaulted member templates value<U=T>() (real throw path -> bad_expected_access) and swap<OT,OE>(), and the non-template error() overload set. tl::unexpected<std::string>/<int> are listed for their REAL non-template ctors (a Python str/int constructs one directly) + value(); tl::bad_expected_access<std::string> for ctor/error()/what() (its thrown form surfaces in Python as RuntimeError('Bad expected access'), differentially checked). The extest fixture supplies factories (every value/error converting ctor is a template, skipped by design) plus thin wrappers over the all-template fronts: the free operator== family, value_or<U>, and map/and_then with fixed C++ callables. KNOWN OUTCOME B at the pinned toolchain+binder, two layers deep: (1) recorded failure = TC-0008, a codegen ICE -- tl's namespace-scope deduction guide `unexpected(E) -> unexpected<E>` lands in bind_free_operators' define_static_array(members_of(^^tl,...)) walk and the Itanium mangler aborts ('Can't mangle a deduction guide name!'); binding ANY tl class triggers it, no consumer-side dodge. (2) Behind it, visible at -fsyntax-only: BINDER-0012 -- unexpected<E> declares `unexpected() = delete;` and the binder binds every public non-template ctor with no is_deleted filter, so the TU hard-errors ('call to deleted constructor'); the unexpected<E> specs cannot be dropped to dodge it because expected<T,E>'s default-instantiable operator=(unexpected<G>&&) member template makes them signature-reachable anyway. Tests/oracle are written for this surface so the run re-runs green once TC-0008 (or a binder-side deduction-guide filter) and BINDER-0012 land.
skipped_features: expected<void, std::string> (DROPPED from the pack: reflecting it is wrong-rejected -- members_of instantiates member bodies, TC-0007 -- and can_substitute on its swap<OT=void> member template SEGVs the compiler, TC-0006; extest has no void factories so discovery cannot re-add it)
all value/error converting constructors + in_place/unexpect tag ctors (templates, skipped by design; extest factories instead)

monadic and_then/map/transform/or_else and value_or (member templates with a non-defaulted F/U parameter -- not default-instantiable; extest wraps map/and_then/value_or with fixed callables as the differential channel)
emplace (parameter-pack member template, skipped by design)
free operator==/!= family and free swap/make_unexpected (free function templates -- not bindable; extest eq_* wrappers cover equality)
operator*/operator-> accessors (unary deref has no Python dunder; value() is the access path)
&&/const&&-qualified value()/error()/unexpected::value() overloads (binder qualifier matrix skips rvalue-ref-qualified)
